key_insight: The paper shows that effective world models and action spaces can be learned directly from unlabeled, in-the-wild videos by discovering latent action variables and training dynamics in that latent space, enabling prediction and planning without ground-truth action labels.
problem_solved: Removes the reliance on expensive or unavailable action labels for building predictive world models, enabling agents to learn how actions affect the world from noisy, real-world video data.
method: Learn a compact latent action representation from raw video (frames or frame-pairs) in an unsupervised way so actions are encoded without supervision.
Train a dynamics/world model that predicts future latent states conditioned on the discovered latent actions, allowing rollouts and planning in latent space.
Enforce disentanglement and plausibility (e.g., via reconstruction/prediction objectives and regularization) so action latents capture controllable effects while separating nuisance factors.
impact: Allows practitioners to build predictive models and planners using large-scale, unlabeled video corpora, reducing labeling cost and broadening applicability of model-based RL and planning to real-world data.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: in-the-wild video -> latent action encoder -> latent dynamics/world model -> predicted future frames/rollouts
Before/after disentanglement: side-by-side comparison showing controllable changes captured by action latents versus static/nuisance factors
Rollout gallery: sequences of predicted futures under different sampled latent actions to illustrate planning and counterfactuals
Icon set: video camera (data), gear/latent vector (learned actions), forward arrow/paths (prediction & planning)
paper_title: Learning Latent Action World Models In The Wild
paper_authors: Quentin Garrido, Tushar Nagarajan, Basile Terver, Nicolas Ballas, Yann LeCun
